# View Manager Builder Column Layout Implementation Plan

> **For Claude:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task.

**Goal:** Lay the builder transient's five infix groups (Type / Time / Structural / Metadata / Prefix) out in side-by-side columns arranged as two horizontal rows instead of one tall vertical stack, so the builder is wider and shorter and uses more of the transient's horizontal space.

**Architecture:** The builder is a `transient-define-prefix` generated by the macro `org-gtd-view-manager--define-builder-transient` in `org-gtd-view-manager.el`. Today the macro splices its five per-group vectors flat (`,@columns`), which transient renders as five stacked single-column groups. In transient, a group whose *first child is itself a vector* is classed `transient-columns` and renders its child vectors side by side. The fix wraps the per-group vectors into two outer "row" vectors (3 groups over 2 groups) and splices those instead. This is a purely visual rearrangement: no suffix command, key letter, reader, formatter, or `--set-value` wiring changes.

**Tech Stack:** Emacs Lisp, `transient.el` 0.13.5 (vendored under `.eldev/`), e-unit test framework.

**Yaks issue:** `view-manager-builder-spread-infix-groups-across-horizontal-space-urp5`

## Recommended Column Arrangement: 3 + 2 (two rows)

**Row 1 (side by side): Type · Time · Structural**
**Row 2 (side by side): Metadata · Prefix**

Group sizes (infix count): Type = 1, Time = 3, Structural = 4, Metadata = 5, Prefix = 2 (15 infixes total).

**Rationale:**
- **Fits an 80-column terminal with margin.** Each infix line is `"%-13s %s"` (a 13-char label plus a short value, usually `—`) prefixed by a 1-char key — roughly 17-19 columns wide per column including transient's inter-column padding. A row of 3 (Type/Time/Structural) is ~58 cols; a row of 2 (Metadata/Prefix) is ~38 cols. Both clear 80 comfortably. A single row of all five would be ~95-100 cols, which overflows an 80-col terminal and is tight even at 100 — rejected.
- **Preserves reading order.** Groups stay in their natural `groups`-alist order left-to-right, top-to-bottom: Type → Time → Structural, then Metadata → Prefix. No cognitive reshuffle for existing users.
- **Roughly balances column height.** Row 1's tallest column is Structural (4 infixes); Row 2's is Metadata (5). The infix area shrinks from ~20 lines (5 stacked groups + headers) to ~11 lines (2 rows), which is the whole point of the issue.
- **Simplest split that reads cleanly.** 2+2+1 also fits but adds a third row for no readability gain; 5-in-a-row is too wide. 3+2 is the sweet spot.

The summary line `[:description ...]` stays pinned at the top and the `["Actions" ...]` group stays at the bottom; only the five infix groups are rearranged.

## Testability: what is headless vs manual

- **Manual-only (visual):** that the groups actually *render* side by side across the width. Transient column layout is a rendering property; there is no headless assertion for "these appear in the same row." Covered by the manual re-QA step in Task 3.
- **Headless (structural invariants) — MUST have tests:** that the rearrangement **drops no infix** and the prefix still compiles and is `fboundp`. These are real, checkable guards using `ogt--transient-suffix-plist` (defined in `test/helpers/utils.el`, loaded transitively by `ogt-eunit-prelude`, so no extra `require` is needed in the test file). Covered by Task 1.

**Framing note (important):** the "every key still bound" test is a **regression guard**, not a classic red→green driver. It is expected to be **green from the start** (the keys are already bound today). Its value is proving that *after* the layout change the keys are *still* bound — i.e. that reshaping the groups into columns didn't silently drop an infix. Task 1 adds it and confirms green on today's code; Task 2 changes the layout and confirms it stays green. An optional teeth-check step is included to demonstrate the guard *can* go red.

## Task 1: Add the structural regression guard (green-from-start)

**Files:**
- Modify: `test/unit/view-manager-build-test.el`

**Step 1: Write the guard test**

Add this `deftest` to `test/unit/view-manager-build-test.el`, immediately after the existing `view-manager-build/has-type-infix` test (before `view-manager-build/save-rejects-blank-name`):

```elisp
(deftest view-manager-build/every-infix-and-action-key-is-bound ()
  "Every generated infix key and every action key stays bound.
Regression guard for the multi-column layout: rearranging the five
infix groups into side-by-side columns must not drop any infix.  Keys
are read from `org-gtd-view-manager--filter-specs' so this can never
drift from the single source of truth the builder is generated from."
  (dolist (entry org-gtd-view-manager--filter-specs)
    (let* ((key (plist-get (cdr entry) :key))
           (plist (ogt--transient-suffix-plist
                   'org-gtd-view-manager--build key)))
      (assert-equal key (plist-get plist :key))))
  (dolist (key '("RET" "s" "C-c C-k"))
    (let ((plist (ogt--transient-suffix-plist
                  'org-gtd-view-manager--build key)))
      (assert-equal key (plist-get plist :key)))))
```

Why data-driven over `org-gtd-view-manager--filter-specs`: it asserts **all 15** generated infix keys (`t w D C o O N H A e W G P x X`) survive, plus the three action keys (`RET s C-c C-k`), without hardcoding a list that could rot. This is stronger than adding one representative key per group.

**Step 2: Run the test to confirm it passes (guard is green on current code)**

Run: `.claude/skills/test/run-tests.sh test/unit/view-manager-build-test.el`
Expected: `PASS: N tests ...` with N one greater than before, no failures. (This guard passes today — that's expected; see the framing note above.)

**Step 3 (OPTIONAL sanity check — prove the guard has teeth, then REVERT):**

To confirm the test would actually catch a dropped infix, temporarily make the macro drop the Prefix group: in `org-gtd-view-manager.el`, in `org-gtd-view-manager--define-builder-transient`, change the `groups` alist to omit `(prefix . "Prefix")`, then run the same command. Expected: **FAIL** on keys `x` / `X` (Prefix infixes gone). Then `git checkout -- org-gtd-view-manager.el` to fully revert this experiment. Do NOT keep this change.

**Step 4: Commit is deferred** — this test and the Task 2 layout change ship in ONE commit (see Task 3). Do not commit yet.

## Task 2: Rearrange the five infix groups into two rows of columns

**Files:**
- Modify: `org-gtd-view-manager.el` — the `let*` bindings and body of `org-gtd-view-manager--define-builder-transient` (around lines 689-742).

**Step 1: Add a `rows` binding that wraps the per-group vectors into two row vectors**

In the macro's `let*` binding list, the `columns` binding currently ends the bindings. It looks like this (the three trailing parens close `mapcar`, the `columns` binding, and the whole `let*` binding list):

```elisp
         (columns
          (mapcar
           (lambda (grp)
             (apply
              #'vector
              (cdr grp)
              (delq nil
                    (mapcar
                     (lambda (entry)
                       (when (eq (plist-get (cdr entry) :group) (car grp))
                         (let* ((dsl-key (car entry))
                                (letter (plist-get (cdr entry) :key))
                                (name (intern
                                       (format "org-gtd-view-manager--set-%s"
                                               dsl-key)))
                                (label (symbol-name dsl-key)))
                           (list letter
                                 `(lambda ()
                                    (org-gtd-view-manager--infix-description
                                     ',dsl-key ,label))
                                 name
                                 :transient t))))
                     org-gtd-view-manager--filter-specs))))
           groups)))
    `(progn
```

Change the last two lines of that block — `           groups)))` and `    \`(progn` — so that `columns`'s binding closes with only two parens, a new `rows` binding is added, then the binding list closes. Replace:

```elisp
           groups)))
    `(progn
```

with:

```elisp
           groups))
         ;; Lay the five infix groups out as two side-by-side ROWS instead of
         ;; one tall stack.  In transient, a group whose first child is itself
         ;; a vector is classed `transient-columns' and renders its child
         ;; vectors side by side (see `transient--parse-group').  Wrapping each
         ;; row's per-group vectors in an OUTER vector produces that layout.
         ;; Row 1: Type Time Structural (columns 0 1 2).  Row 2: Metadata
         ;; Prefix (columns 3 4).  Indices track the `groups' alist order.
         (rows
          (list (apply #'vector (list (nth 0 columns)
                                      (nth 1 columns)
                                      (nth 2 columns)))
                (apply #'vector (list (nth 3 columns)
                                      (nth 4 columns))))))
    `(progn
```

Notes for the implementer:
- `(nth 0 columns)` … `(nth 4 columns)` are the five per-group vectors in `groups` order (Type, Time, Structural, Metadata, Prefix). `(apply #'vector (list vecA vecB vecC))` returns `[vecA vecB vecC]` — an outer vector whose children are the group vectors, i.e. one row of columns.
- `rows` is therefore a two-element list: `([TypeVec TimeVec StructVec] [MetaVec PrefixVec])`.
- Paren balance is easy to get wrong by hand — do **not** eyeball it; the compile in Step 3 will catch any imbalance immediately.

**Step 2: Splice `rows` instead of `columns` in the prefix body**

In the same macro, the generated prefix body currently reads:

```elisp
         [:description (lambda () (org-gtd-view-manager--build-summary))]
         ,@columns
         ["Actions"
```

Change `,@columns` to `,@rows`:

```elisp
         [:description (lambda () (org-gtd-view-manager--build-summary))]
         ,@rows
         ["Actions"
```

This is the ONLY body change. The `[:description ...]` summary stays first; `["Actions" ...]` stays last. `,@rows` splices the two row vectors as two top-level groups between them.

**Step 3: Recompile with warnings-as-errors, then restore `dir`**

Run:
```bash
~/bin/eldev compile --warnings-as-errors
git checkout -- dir
```
Expected: compilation succeeds with **no errors and no warnings** (warnings are errors). If it fails with an "End of file during parsing" / unbalanced-parens error, re-check the paren count of the `rows` binding from Step 1. After a clean compile, `git checkout -- dir` restores the Info `dir` file the compile deleted.

Reminder: never `git add` `dir` or any `*.elc`. Confirm with `git status` that only `org-gtd-view-manager.el` and `test/unit/view-manager-build-test.el` are staged/modified for the eventual commit (plus the new plan doc if you choose to include it).

**Step 4: Run the guard test — confirm it STAYS green after the layout change**

Run: `.claude/skills/test/run-tests.sh test/unit/view-manager-build-test.el`
Expected: PASS, same count as end of Task 1, no failures. This is the payoff: the layout change reshaped the groups into columns and **every infix key is still bound** — no infix was dropped.

**Step 5: Run the full unit suite to confirm no collateral regression**

Run: `.claude/skills/test/run-tests.sh unit`
Expected: PASS with the full unit count (baseline was 1436 across the whole suite; the unit category is a subset). No failures. Capture the `Seed:` line in case of a flake (per project memory, flakes are usually setup issues, not this change).

## Task 3: Manual re-QA of the visual result (manual-only)

The side-by-side rendering cannot be asserted headlessly — verify it by eye.

**Step 1: Load the changed source into a live Emacs**

Open `org-gtd-view-manager.el` in Emacs and `M-x eval-buffer` (do NOT use a plain file load — Emacs caches, per the project memory note). Ensure a normal org-gtd setup is active (keywords + keyword-mapping + `org-agenda-files`), consistent with the "QA needs a proper org-gtd setup" memory.

**Step 2: Open the builder transient**

`M-x org-gtd-view-manager--build` (or via the view-manager entry point / list transient that launches the builder).

**Step 3: Confirm the layout**

- The **summary line** ("View: Untitled — …") appears at the **top**.
- Below it, **Row 1** shows **Type**, **Time**, and **Structural** as three columns **side by side**.
- Below that, **Row 2** shows **Metadata** and **Prefix** as two columns **side by side**.
- The **Actions** group (`RET Preview`, `s Save`, `C-c C-k Abort`) appears at the **bottom**.
- The builder is visibly **wider and shorter** than before (no longer one tall single column). It fits within an ~80-column frame.

**Step 4: Confirm every key still works**

Press each infix key and confirm it prompts / toggles as before, then aborts cleanly:
- Type: `t`
- Time: `w` `D` `C`
- Structural: `o` `O` `N` `H`
- Metadata: `A` `e` `W` `G` `P`
- Prefix: `x` `X`
- Actions: `RET` (preview refreshes — do not regress P1), `s` (save), `C-c C-k` (abort; window layout restores — do not regress P2)

Spot-check at least one key per group plus all three actions. Confirm the preview still refreshes on change (P1) and that aborting restores the entry window layout (P2).

**Step 5: Commit (single commit for the whole change)**

```bash
git add org-gtd-view-manager.el test/unit/view-manager-build-test.el
git commit -m "feat(view-manager): lay builder infix groups out in two column rows

Render the five builder infix groups (Type/Time/Structural over
Metadata/Prefix) as two rows of side-by-side columns instead of one

Purely visual: keys, readers, formatters and set-value wiring are
unchanged.  Adds a data-driven guard test asserting every filter-spec
key and action key stays bound after the rearrangement.

Fixes: view-manager-builder-spread-infix-groups-across-horizontal-space-urp5"
```
